reviews.title: Excellent Budget AIO With Great Cooling, Quiet Fans, and a Surprisingly Premium Screen
reviews.comment: The Jungle Leopard PF 360 CPU Water AIO turned out to be a much better cooler than I expected for the price. The build quality out of the box feels solid, and installation on my Intel i7‑14700K was straightforward. The kit includes brackets for Intel 115X, 1200, and 1700 sockets, along with AMD mounting hardware. Setting the bracket size for LGA 1700 was simple, and attaching the backplate through the motherboard was just as easy. The pump head bracket twists and locks into place cleanly, and choosing the correct LGA 1700 spacers made securing the pump to the CPU quick and hassle‑free. The included 360mm fans were a pleasant surprise. They’re very quiet, even under load, and the RGB implementation looks fantastic. The 360 fans has four infinity‑mirror accents on the front plus full-length infinity mirrors along both sides, giving the radiator a premium look. I usually replace stock AIO fans, but in this case I don’t feel the need to—the performance and aesthetics are already excellent. Cooling performance is strong as well. At idle, my 14700K sits between 36–46°C across the cores. Under a full 100% burn‑in load, temperatures rise to 60–70°C, and none of the cores hit thermal throttling. For a CPU known to run hot, that’s impressive for an AIO in this price range. The pump‑head screen is another highlight. It’s removable and can be mounted in three different orientations. I chose the vertical position with the tubes entering from the bottom, which limits the screen’s rotation options, but it still ended up exactly how I wanted it. If you want the screen oriented vertically downward, you’ll need the tubes coming in from the side due to the pin alignment—but the flexibility is still better than many AIOs. The software worked with some issues on my system. The interface isn’t immediately intuitive, so I watched a couple of YouTube videos to get familiar with it. Once I understood the layout, I was able to upload video clips or screen captures, add system stats like CPU temperature, and customize the screen with various widgets. It supports multiple image and video formats, and so far it hasn’t conflicted with any of my other RGB software.  One item I noticed if I used some animated videos, the screen saver would not execute for windows.  Since I am concerned about screen burn in, I wanted the screen saver to work so I had to go with still images which did not affect the windows screen saver.  Hopefully this will be addressed in future software updates.  Another option I hope they will add to future software updates is some sort of picture and video shuffle so the screen could change over time. Overall, this AIO delivers excellent cooling, quiet fans, great RGB, and a customizable display—all at a very competitive price. It exceeded my expectations in almost every category.

reviews.title: Unbeatable 5.5" LCD AIO Cooler—IF You Can Get It For $100-$115
reviews.comment: We have tested a massive number of AIO liquid coolers, and the Jungle Leopard PF 360 is an absolute hidden gem. At the right price (specifically around the $100 to $115 mark), we highly recommend this cooler for mid-to-high-end builds. Cooling Hardware: Features a 360mm radiator paired with three 120mm ARGB Infinity Mirror PWM fans (up to 2000 RPM). Performance: In our stress tests, this cooler excels. Under heavy, sustained loads (like 4K video rendering and intense gaming), it easily prevents high-end CPUs from thermal throttling. It manages to keep temperatures incredibly stable while maintaining a surprisingly quiet noise profile. The Screen & Software: The star of the show is the massive 5.5-inch magnetic LCD screen on the pump block. The customization software is extremely intuitive and easy to navigate compared to some of the clunky proprietary apps from bigger brands. If you want to see exactly how to set up the screen and see our full performance testing breakdown, check out the video on our YouTube channel! Bottom line: If you catch this cooler in that $100-$115 sweet spot, do not hesitate to buy it.
